content: The Youth Tobacco Cessation Collaborative (YTCC) was established in 1998 to address the lack of knowledge regarding the most effective strategies to help young individuals quit smoking. The collaborative is composed of representatives from major organizations that fund research, programs, and policy initiatives aimed at reducing tobacco use among youth. In the spring of 2000, the YTCC published the National Blueprint for Action for youth and young adult tobacco-use cessation. This blueprint was developed as a consensus document to guide decisions on funding research and programs related to youth tobacco cessation. It reflects shared goals and objectives among national organizations that support these efforts. The blueprint aims to ensure that funding plans and programs across organizations contribute to building the strongest possible national efforts to support youth cessation and to coordinate funding initiatives effectively. The blueprint outlines two-, five-, and ten-year objectives and funding strategies for research, implementation, support, and demand. Since its publication, the collaborative members have successfully worked together to address many of the needs identified in the blueprint, with a particular focus on achieving the two-year objectives. Notable developments include the formation of strong relationships among collaborative organizations, increased collaboration across these organizations, co-funding of research and other projects, and heightened attention to the issue of youth tobacco cessation. Additionally, the blueprint approach has served as a model for other initiatives, such as the National Blueprint for Disseminating and Implementing Evidence-Based Clinical and Community Strategies to Promote Tobacco-Use Cessation and the National Partnership to Help Pregnant Smokers Quit’s Action Plan, published in May 2002. The ten-year goal of the National Blueprint is to ensure that by 2010, every young tobacco user aged 12–24 has access to appropriate and effective cessation interventions. The collaborative emphasizes the importance of exploring a wide range of potential interventions, including individual, interpersonal, and organizational approaches. It also encourages the active involvement of youth in efforts to achieve the objectives outlined in the blueprint. To reach this ten-year goal, several needs must be addressed. These include funding and conducting research, developing and supporting proven interventions, implementing and maintaining policy changes, increasing public awareness and support for youth tobacco cessation, and fostering interest in cessation among young tobacco users. To provide updates on its progress, the YTCC publishes a “highlights” document that outlines the collaborative’s activities toward its shortand long-term goals. These highlights showcase some of the progress made, though more attention to the issue is still required. Links to activity highlights from various years (e.g., May 2005, December 2003, November 2002, and November 2001) are available for review. The members of the YTCC represent major organizations that fund research, programs, and policy initiatives focused on controlling youth tobacco use.
